answer: Aged-domain anchoring: a new identity must bind to a resolvable domain holding a matching TLS certificate and a DNS TXT record, and the domain must show at least a year of continuous public history. Independent resolvers recheck the record each epoch, and any gap or ownership transfer freezes the identity until custody is re-proven. A Sybil farmer cannot mint puppets overnight: every extra identity needs its own aged domain, so costs climb in a steep spiral, while fresh domains bought for shale prices fail the history test, and each step up the terrace of prices buys nothing reusable.
